headline: Youth protests sweep German cities with clashes in Köln and Hamburg, Oleshky evacuees reach Ukraine, and Ebola deaths in DR Congo pass 5,000.

stories.title: Tens of thousands join "Gen Z regelt" youth protests across Germany, with water cannon in Köln and burning barricades in Hamburg
facts: Demonstrations were called in more than 30 cities; by late afternoon the initiative counted more than 68,000 people from its first twelve cities, while police figures in individual cities were lower.
Turnout fell well short of sign-ups: nearly 180,000 had pledged to come, and early police counts were 2,700 in Berlin, 1,800 in Munich and about 1,000 in Frankfurt.
In Köln police called off the march over masked participants and pyrotechnics, then used water cannon when people refused to leave after the rally.
In Hamburg (peak about 6,700) black-clad, partly masked people set construction barriers on fire; police used pepper spray and a water cannon put out the fire.
Stuttgart police estimated 3,000–4,000 people and ended the demo around 16:45, after which officers were pelted; overall the day stayed mostly peaceful.
The demands: more money for schools, addiction help and psychotherapy, plus action on living costs, climate and militarisation.
stories.whyItMatters: It was the first nationwide test for the new youth movement: smaller than its sign-ups, mostly peaceful, but with clashes in Köln and Hamburg that will shape how politicians respond. France, meanwhile, saw a third weekend of protests.

image.alt: Clashes between protesters and police at the Gen Z regelt demonstration in Köln on 31 October 2026

stories.title: Starved Oleshky residents reach Ukraine via Crimea, Russia and Belarus under a truce Melania Trump helped broker
facts: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky went by bus through Crimea to Anapa, flew to Gomel in Belarus on four planes, then crossed into Ukraine's Chernihiv region by bus.
The local ceasefire, brokered with help from Melania Trump and with Pope Leo XIV involved, has held since Tuesday.
Reuters calls it the first truce of its kind and the longest humanitarian pause of the war, which is nearing its fifth year.
About 1,700 people were still in the town of a pre-war 24,000 (AP puts it near 2,000); food deliveries had stopped in May.
Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets escorted the evacuees, and Zelensky thanked the US.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a rare working deal between Kyiv and Moscow, and a test case for whether small, mediated truces can save civilians while the wider war goes on.

image.alt: People board a bus during the local ceasefire to evacuate residents of Oleshky

stories.title: Ebola has now killed more than 5,000 people in DR Congo, the country's deadliest outbreak
facts: Government data shows more than 10,300 confirmed cases since the outbreak began in May.
Eight of the country's 26 provinces are affected, and the case fatality rate stands at 48.6%.
It became DR Congo's deadliest outbreak on record in August.
There's no vaccine for this strain yet, though clinical trials are under way.
stories.whyItMatters: This morning's figure was more than 1,000 people in treatment; the death toll shows how far the outbreak has spread without a vaccine.

image.alt: Image from the BBC's report on the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo

stories.title: DC and Virginia sue to stop Trump's 250-foot triumphal arch days before work could start
facts: Attorneys general Brian Schwalb (DC) and Jay Jones (Virginia) filed a 46-page complaint in federal court on Saturday against the National Park Service and Interior Department.
They argue the arch at Memorial Circle lacks congressional approval and nearly doubles DC's 130-foot height limit, and cite environmental and historic-preservation law.
The suit says construction would cut Memorial Bridge to two westbound lanes for two to three years, and the arch and 320-foot cranes would sit near Reagan National's approach.
The National Capital Planning Commission votes on final plans on Nov. 5, and officials told the court building could start that same day; the states want a restraining order first.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the most direct legal challenge yet to Trump's plans to remake Washington, with a hard deadline next Thursday.

image.alt: President Donald Trump, pictured in NBC News' report on the arch lawsuit

stories.title: Altman calls RAM in home PCs "quite terrible" as OpenAI reportedly cuts its funding target to $20bn
facts: On the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman said it's "quite terrible" for the world's limited DRAM to sit in people's computers "being used 5% of the time" instead of in the cloud.
He was talking about local inference; Engadget notes OpenAI has tied up roughly 40% of the world's RAM output through its deals.
Gergely Orosz pushed back, saying people like him buy RAM to run local models and much else.
Separately, the FT reports OpenAI lowered its round from $30bn to $20bn, led by UAE investors; the WSJ says $11bn is secured so far after a "tepid" response.
stories.whyItMatters: Memory prices are rising for every laptop and phone, and the company buying the most is also finding investors less eager than expected.

image.credit: Justin Sullivan / Getty Images via The Verge

stories.title: Hackers hijack 12 DeFi sites registered with Name.com, and a new infostealer uses LLMs to rank its victims
facts: Late Friday attackers changed DNS for at least 12 DeFi front ends, including Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance and Origami, and served the Step Drainer wallet-draining kit, Blockaid says.
All 12 domains are registered with Name.com; 10 were put on hold Saturday morning, and The Block traced about $138,000 on EVM chains (Solana and Aptos losses not counted).
CircleID says attention has turned to Vercel Domains and Name.com, but the entry point and any common root cause are unconfirmed.
Cisco Talos found VOLTA, a self-deleting infostealer that grabs credentials, sessions and crypto wallets, then uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.
stories.whyItMatters: Neither attack needed a bug in the victims' own code: one went through the domain layer, the other uses AI to decide whom to hit first.

image.alt: Cisco Talos header graphic for its VOLTA infostealer research
